summary.en: Drone strikes are now a major source of fatalities, with Sudan drones responsible for nearly three quarters of war deaths this year and South Sudan accusing Sudan of a drone attack that killed scores in a disputed area. A priest who had fled South Sudan was murdered in Birmingham, and a pastor was jailed in South Sudan for performing a Christian song with musical instruments. The government screened out 54 children from a police recruitment drive, and SPLM Jonglei chairperson candidates began their race without primaries in Pigi County, while a chairperson was injured in a road incident. Protesters demanded inclusion in the UNISFA mandate drafting, and UCDP recorded two battle-related deaths in 2024.
summary.nb: Droneangrep er nå en viktig kilde til dødsfall, med sudanske droner ansvarlige for nesten tre fjerdedeler av krigsdødsfallene i år, og Sør-Sudan anklager Sudan for et droneangrep som drepte mange i et omstridt område. En prest som hadde flyktet fra Sør-Sudan ble drept i Birmingham, og en pastor ble fengslet i Sør-Sudan for å ha fremført en kristen sang med musikkinstrumenter. Regjeringen screente ut 54 barn fra en politirekrutteringskampanje, og kandidater til SPLM Jonglei-styre i Pigi fylke startet sin kamp uten primærvalg, mens en styreleder ble skadet i en veitrafikkulykke. Demonstranter krevde medvirkning i utarbeidelsen av mandatet til UNISFA, og UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i kamper i 2024.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
